title: G-equivariant (co)sheaf of subgroups and characters
body_html:
$G$-equivariant (co)sheaf of subgroups and characters

Assume $G$ is a subgroup of a larger group $M$, and $G$ acts cellularly on the regular CW complex $X$.

Definition (sheaf/cosheaf of subgroups). A $G$-equivariant sheaf (resp.\ cosheaf) $K$ on $X$ of subgroups of $M$ is a $G$-equivariant sheaf (resp.\ cosheaf) of groups on $X$ with:

  • $K_E \le M$ for every $E \in [\![X]\!]$;
  • $r^K_{E,E'}$ is the inclusion $K_E \hookrightarrow K_{E'}$ (sheaf case: $E \preceq E'$; cosheaf case: $E' \preceq E$);
  • $K_{gE} = g K_E g^{-1}$ and $a^K_{g,E}$ is conjugation by $g$.

Equivalently $K$ is an object of $\Cosh_G(X,\mathrm{Sub}(M))$, where $\mathrm{Sub}(M)$ is the category of subgroups of $M$ with group homomorphisms.

Definition (character). A character of $K$ is a family $\phi = \{\phi_E\}_{E \in [\![X]\!]}$ with $\phi_E \in \Hom(K_E, R^\times)$ satisfying

  • compatibility: $\phi_E |_{K_{E'}} = \phi_{E'}$ along restrictions;
  • equivariance: $\phi_{gE}(g u g^{-1}) = \phi_E(u)$ for $g \in G$.

Standard examples

  • $E \mapsto \Fix_G(E)$ is always a cosheaf of subgroups of $G$.
  • $E \mapsto \Stab_G(E)$ is not in general a cosheaf, but it becomes one after refining the CW structure so that $\Stab_G(E) = \Fix_G(E)$ for every cell.
  • For $X = \mathcal{B}(G)$ (the Bruhat–Tits building of a reductive $G$ over a local field, with the standard polysimplicial structure), $x \mapsto G_{x,0}$ is a cosheaf and $x \mapsto G_{x,0+}$ is a sheaf. After refining to the polyhedral structure of [BT2], the same is true of $x \mapsto G_{x,r}$ and $x \mapsto G_{x,r+}$ for $r \in \tfrac{1}{n}\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$.

Two derived (co)sheaves

Given a sheaf $K$ of subgroups, a character $\phi$ of $K$, and an $R[G]$-module $V$, both of the following are objects of $\Cosh_G(X,R)$ resp.\ $\Sh_G(X,R)$:

  • $\widetilde V : E \mapsto V[\phi_E]$ — the $\phi_E$-isotypic submodule of $V$, viewed as a cosheaf;
  • $\widetilde{\widetilde V} : E \mapsto V_{\phi_E}$ — the $\phi_E$-isotypic quotient of $V$, viewed as a sheaf.

These are the building blocks of Schneider–Stuhler theory and recur in The subcategory Rep_φ(G).
